recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中央是一顆循環芽細胞：比淋巴球略大、核質比很高、染色質細緻均勻並有淡色核仁、周圍只有一圈藍色無顆粒胞質；在全血球減少病人的周邊血看到芽細胞，要想到MDS伴過多芽細胞。
features: Single circulating blast of intermediate size, larger than a small lymphocyte
Very high N:C ratio with a thin rim of pale-blue agranular cytoplasm
Round to slightly irregular nucleus with finely dispersed chromatin and faint nucleoli
No Auer rods or cytoplasmic granules
Background red cells with mild anisopoikilocytosis (occasional elliptocytes/teardrop forms); platelets sparse
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a circulating blast of intermediate size with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, faint nucleoli and a thin rim of agranular basophilic cytoplasm; no Auer rods are identified. Red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional elliptocytes, and platelets are sparse. Dysplastic neutrophils are not captured in this field. In a pancytopenic patient with 2% circulating blasts, these findings are consistent with a myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts, and bone marrow examination with flow cytometry is required for classification.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells and more condensed chromatin without the fine blastic pattern.
LGLs have abundant pale cytoplasm with azurophilic granules and mature clumped chromatin.
AML is defined by ≥20% blasts in blood or marrow, whereas rare blasts with pancytopenia favor MDS pending marrow count.
Lymphoma cells often have cleaved or irregular nuclei with coarser chromatin and show a mature B- or T-cell phenotype rather than CD34/CD117 positivity.
